prompt:
A wide empty churchyard at night, painted in a warm hand-illustrated storybook style with clean flat shapes and soft painted shading — no photorealism, no line art, no text, no watermark. Landscape, about twice as wide as it is tall.

THERE IS NO CHURCH IN THIS IMAGE. NO BUILDING OF ANY KIND — no chapel, no steeple, no spire, no roof, no walls, no door, no windows, no ruins, no gravestones, no fence, no gate, no signpost. NO PEOPLE, no animals, no lamp posts, no benches, no flowers and no planted beds. NO PATH, no walkway, no paving, no track and no road. This is only the empty ground and the sky behind everything else, and the entire MIDDLE of the frame must stay plain and uncluttered — a church building and a path are drawn on top of it later and must not land on top of anything.

Two bands and nothing else. The upper two thirds is a deep violet-purple night sky, darkest at the edges and a little warmer and lighter toward the top centre, with a soft haze near the horizon. NO STARS AND NO MOON — stars are added separately and would double up. The lower third is a dark blue-green lawn of neatly kept grass running flat away from the viewer, slightly cooler and darker at the very bottom edge. The horizon where they meet sits about two thirds of the way down.

Along that horizon, and ONLY along it, a low soft line of distant trees in silhouette — a treeline far away, no taller than a tenth of the image, dark and simple with no individual branches, sitting well to the LEFT and RIGHT of centre and thinning out toward the middle so the centre of the horizon stays open sky.

Palette: deep violet and indigo for the sky, dark blue-green for the grass, everything muted and low-contrast so that brighter objects drawn on top of it read clearly. Nothing in this image should draw the eye — it is a backdrop.
